title: Man. Post. Cap. II §XIV: Garissoles — subject distinction; 2nd vs 3rd coincide
pass_a_gloss: GAR. But also in this distinction of the subject some things are contained which to one weighing well it is scarcely possible that they can be approved. For 1. With what fruit is the second signification of Adam's sin distinguished from the third, when whatever is here said of Adam's sin in the second signification is asserted to agree with it in reality, not insofar as it is a transient action, but insofar as it is habitual and permanent corruption? For so Adam's sin said in the second and third mode coincide in the same thing in reality.
pass_b_english: Garissoles: But in this distinction of the subject as well there are points that, well weighed, can scarcely be approved. For (1) what is gained by distinguishing the second sense of Adam's sin from the third, when whatever is said here of Adam's sin in the second sense is claimed to fit it in reality not as a passing act but as habitual, lasting corruption? So Adam's sin in the second and third modes really coincides in the same thing.
source_text: GAR. Sed & in hac subjecti distinctione nonnulla continentur, quae bene perpendenti vix est ut probari valeant. Nam 1. Quo fructu secunda peccati Adae significatio distinguitur a tertia, cum quicquid de peccato Adae in secunda significatione hic dicitur, ei reapse convenire asseratur, non quatenus est actio transiens, sed quatenus est corruptio habitualis & permanens? Ita enim peccatum Adae secundo & tertio modo dictum in idem revera coincidunt.

lemmas.gloss: really coincide in the same thing

choices.choice: Second vs third signification coincide in habitual corruption
